newsitem.title: ITALY: ITALY'S ENI TO CUT PUMP PRICES FROM TUES.
newsitem.headline: ITALY'S ENI TO CUT PUMP PRICES FROM TUES.

text.p: Italian energy group Eni said on Monday its petrol distributors Agip Petroli and IP, would reduce their petrol and diesel prices by 10 lire a litre from Tuesday.
Italian oil firms came under strong criticism from the government last week for immediately hiking pump prices in response to recent dollar gains.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi complained that the increases meant Italian petrol was the most costly in the European Union.
State-controlled Eni said in a statement it had decided to cut tariffs following a recent dip in crude prices and a slightly weaker dollar.
The lira on Monday was trading at around 1,810 against the U.S. currency, down from highs of around 1,850 last week.
Eni's tariff reduction will bring the price of Agip and IP leaded petrol to 1,920 lire per litre while a litre of unleaded petrol will cost 1,830 lire.
